name: Character Talks
description: The workhorse: one chibi archetype (officer, general, soldier, sailor, pilot, diplomat, civilian, nurse or the historian host) talks to camera with lip-sync, blinks, bounces and gesture beats on a painted location (war room, trench, airfield, city, office, alps, sea…). Optional chunky thumbnail text slams in on its keyword, with a date tag and the nation's flag.

role.description: Who talks. The same role+nation pair must look identical across the video.

nation.description: Nation — defines flag and uniform colours.

location.description: Location. Keep it consistent between neighbouring scenes.

text.description: Optional chunky thumbnail text (1–5 words, e.g. 'WHY NOT THEM?'). Wrap one word in *asterisks* to colour it.

kicker.description: Optional tiny tag above the text (1–3 words).

keyword.description: Narration word on which the text and key gesture land (must appear in the narration).

prop.description: Optional prop held in the right hand.

gesture.description: Gesture on the keyword (default: role's signature move).

word.description: Narration word the beat lands on.

side.description: Which side the character stands on when there is text (default left).

label.description: Optional name chip under the character (e.g. 'BRITAIN', 'THE GENERAL').

closeUp.description: Cut to a close-up for the second half (default true).

captions.description: Word-synced captions at the bottom (default false).

exampleNarration: By the summer of 1940, the staff officers had a map, a plan for almost everyone, and one very awkward question. Why not Switzerland? It was right there, in the middle of everything, and nobody could quite agree on what to do about it.

name: Two Sides
description: Split screen with a jagged divider: each side has its own location, chibi and waving flag. Lines of narration alternate between the two sides — the speaker pops forward, the other side dims and reacts — with a speech bubble per line. The signature 'told from both sides' framing.

role.description: Archetype by uniform (never a real person).

nation.description: Nation — defines flag and uniform colours.

role.description: Archetype by uniform (never a real person).

nation.description: Nation — defines flag and uniform colours.

night.description: Night tint for the right location.

lines.description: 2–6 lines, the exact narration wording, alternating sides.

location.description: Shared default location for both halves.

title.description: Optional short title shown before the first line (≤ 4 words).

exampleNarration: Here is how both sides saw it. We sent eight letters. We did not reply. Not even a postcard? Not even a postcard.

name: War Map
description: A stylised parchment map of Europe: regions colour in with their flags, jagged front lines draw on, chunky arrows advance and red targets lock on — each on its narration word — while a small general in the corner explains with lip-sync. Optional title, date tag and caption.

kicker.description: Optional tiny tag above the title.

regions.description: Regions to colour (0–8), in narration order.

name.description: Region name. One of the named map points: britain, london, ireland, france, paris, spain, madrid, portugal, germany, berlin, switzerland, bern, alps, italy, rome, sicily, scandinavia, sweden, stockholm, norway, denmark, poland, warsaw, ussr, russia, moscow, balkans, greece, austria, vienna, netherlands, belgium, finland, baltic, north-sea, mediterranean, atlantic, channel, turkey, africa, egypt, north-africa.

focus.description: Camera drifts toward the first arrow's end (default true).

exampleNarration: Look at the map. Germany here, Britain here, and tiny neutral Switzerland in the middle. The bombers took off at night, flew toward Germany, and dropped their load on the wrong country. Navigation was optimistic.

name: Diplomacy Desk
description: The 'no reply' gag: in a diplomatic office a sender fires off letters or telegrams one by one (each on its narration word) that pile up on the receiver's desk while the receiver naps, shrugs or smirks. A counter ticks up, then a rubber stamp slams: NO REPLY — or, with reply: true, one answer finally flies back.

role.description: Archetype by uniform (never a real person).

nation.description: Nation — defines flag and uniform colours.

role.description: Archetype by uniform (never a real person).

nation.description: Nation — defines flag and uniform colours.

words.description: Narration words, one per letter, in order (optional).

reply.description: If true one reply finally comes back (default false = NO REPLY stamp).

replyWord.description: Narration word on which the reply arrives.

stamp.description: Stamp text (default 'NO REPLY'; with reply e.g. 'FINALLY').

exampleNarration: So London wrote a letter. Then a second. A third. A fourth. A fifth, slightly more polite. And the answer from Moscow was the same every single time: absolutely nothing.

name: Headline Thumb
description: Thumbnail-style hook frame: diagonal flag-colour stripes, one big chibi reacting (sweat drop, hands on head, anger mark) and giant chunky two-line text that slams in with a flash and a shake on its word. Optional red target circle, date tag and sub-caption.

title.description: The chunky headline (2–6 words, e.g. 'THE WRONG TARGET'). Wrap one word in *asterisks*.

kicker.description: Optional tiny tag above the headline.

word.description: Narration word the headline lands on.

role.description: Archetype by uniform (never a real person).

nation.description: Nation — defines flag and uniform colours.

target.description: Red target circle locks onto the character.

titleColor.description: CSS colour for the headline text (default white).

flag.description: Flag on a pole behind the character (default true).

exampleProps.title: The *wrong* target
exampleProps.sub: How a map error nearly started a second war

exampleNarration: This is the story of a proud bomber crew, a very confident navigator, and the wrong target. Because the city they hit that morning was not in Germany at all.

name: Date Card
description: Chapter opener: a giant date tag slams onto flag-striped paper, the chapter title pops under it, a place chip appears, planes cross the sky and a chibi peeks up from the bottom corner to wave. Use it to open each chapter or jump in time.

word.description: Narration word the title lands on.

nation.description: Nation for the stripes, the flag and the peeking chibi.

role.description: Role of the peeking chibi (default soldier).

exampleNarration: October 1945. The war is over, the borders are quiet, and in Bern a very patient clerk is about to send eight letters and receive no reply.

name: Versus Forces
description: Numbers and equipment comparison on a jagged split screen: two flags, a VS badge, and rows of soldier / tank / plane / bomber / ship pictograms that pop in while the numbers count up — each row on its narration word. Two small generals at the bottom react (proud vs worried).

kicker.description: Optional tiny tag above the title.

nation.description: Nation — defines flag and uniform colours.
Nation — defines flag and uniform colours.

exampleNarration: On paper it was not close. Four hundred thirty thousand Swiss soldiers against four and a half million. A few hundred aircraft against thousands. And twenty four tanks. Twenty four. But the mountains do not read spreadsheets.

name: Neutral Question
description: A puzzled officer holds a map while the camera zooms onto a neutral country: the aggressor's regions colour in, an arrow nudges toward the border and stops, question marks sprout over the country and the chibi shrugs as a chunky 'WHY NOT?' slams in. The 'why didn't they invade…' beat.

country.description: The neutral country on the map (default switzerland). One of the named map points: britain, london, ireland, france, paris, spain, madrid, portugal, germany, berlin, switzerland, bern, alps, italy, rome, sicily, scandinavia, sweden, stockholm, norway, denmark, poland, warsaw, ussr, russia, moscow, balkans, greece, austria, vienna, netherlands, belgium, finland, baltic, north-sea, mediterranean, atlantic, channel, turkey, africa, egypt, north-africa.

countryNation.description: Nation id for the country's flag (default: same as country).

aggressor.description: Who is wondering (colours the surrounding regions, the officer's uniform).

aggressorRegions.description: Map regions to colour in the aggressor's colour (default: the aggressor itself).

items.description: Region. One of the named map points: britain, london, ireland, france, paris, spain, madrid, portugal, germany, berlin, switzerland, bern, alps, italy, rome, sicily, scandinavia, sweden, stockholm, norway, denmark, poland, warsaw, ussr, russia, moscow, balkans, greece, austria, vienna, netherlands, belgium, finland, baltic, north-sea, mediterranean, atlantic, channel, turkey, africa, egypt, north-africa.

question.description: Chunky question text (1–4 words, default 'WHY NOT?').

kicker.description: Optional tiny tag above the question.

word.description: Narration word the question lands on.

prop.description: Prop held before the shrug (default map).

exampleProps.question: Why *not*?
exampleProps.caption: Mountains, tunnels and a very annoying plan

exampleNarration: Germany had France. Germany had Austria. Germany had basically everyone around it. So why not Switzerland? The officers stared at the map, and the map stared back.

name: Timeline
description: A road-style timeline with date tags and label cards that pop up one by one on their narration words, while a small chibi marches along the road and cheers at each stop. Optional flags at events.

kicker.description: Optional tiny tag above the title.

exampleNarration: In January the first letter went out. In March a polite reminder. In June a less polite reminder. And by October, still no reply at all.

name: Crowd Scene
description: Many small chibis at once: a cheering street crowd with bunting and hand flags, soldiers marching across the frame, or an anxious waiting crowd — with a bigger leader in front narrating. Chunky text can land on a word.

items.description: Archetype by uniform (never a real person).

mood.description: cheer (hopping, flags), march (soldiers march across), wait (anxious).

role.description: Archetype by uniform (never a real person).

nation.description: Nation — defines flag and uniform colours.

word.description: Narration word the text and the crowd reaction land on.

exampleNarration: And then, one morning in May, the radio said the words everyone had waited six years to hear. It's over. The streets filled in minutes.

name: Aftermath Reflection
description: Quiet, non-graphic ending: a lone chibi stands hat-in-hand in a dusk field of poppies (or the alps, the sea, a night city), birds cross the sky, the camera drifts slowly and reflective lines fade in one by one. Vignette and a softer palette. Use once, at the end of a chapter or the video.

nation.description: Nation — defines flag and uniform colours.

location.description: field (poppies at dusk), alps, sea or city (night).

lines.description: 1–4 short reflective lines (exact narration wording, ≤ 10 words each).

title.description: Optional closing title (≤ 4 words) near the end.

endExpression.description: Expression for the last third (default calm).

hatOff.description: Hold the hat in hand (default true).

exampleNarration: The letters were never answered. But the border stayed quiet. And that, in 1945, was enough.
